title: Newton’s Method
summary: General real root of f(x) = 0. Edit the green f(M). 51 bytes plus the function.

body.text: No solver key. This WebCal Newton I listing approximates f′ with a 10⁻⁷ step, so you do not type a derivative. The green M³ − 2M − 1 is f(M); change only that expression (variable must stay M). Prompt is the first guess. Each EXE is the next iterate. AC when the digits freeze. E is EXP, so E−7 is 10⁻⁷.

body.label: Memory / run mode
body.text: 51 bytes plus the function of the shared 680-byte pool. Create the slot in COMP. Type ? → : ◢ Goto Lbl If Then from SHIFT 3 (P-CMD).

body.caption: y = x³ − 2x − 1. Guess 1; the first Newton step lands at 3, then walks to ≈ 1.618.

body.text: Question: Use this program to solve the case: x³ − 2x − 1 = 0, guess 1.
Given: Leave the listing as shipped. The unique real root is the golden-ratio value 2 cos(π/5) ≈ 1.618034.

items: Keep 【EXE】. By the sixth pause the display is 1.618034049

body.text: Question: Use this program to solve the case: Same polynomial, guess 0.
Given: A worse start still converges, just with more steps.

items: 0 【EXE】, then 【EXE】 until the digits stop changing

body.text: Question: Use this program to solve the case: Change f — here x² − 2 = 0.
Given: While editing, replace M³−2M−1 with M²−2. Guess 1 for √2.

items: Edit the green expression only. Variable stays M
Guess −1 if you want the negative root

body.label: Pitfalls
body.text: First iterate can jump (1 → 3 on the shipped f). If f′ is nearly 0 you get Math ERROR or a wild jump — try another guess. ClrMemory wipes A–D, X, Y, M; swap it for 0→B if you must keep a constant in another letter. Source: WebCal newton.htm.
